tools.name: required_fte
tools.description: For questions like "how many people do I need" or "how many FTE does this workload take": cases, tickets, claims, orders or any work measured as volume times handling time. Applies shrinkage and target occupancy together; leaving out occupancy understates the people needed by about 15% at the 85% de

tools.name: hiring_plan
tools.description: For hiring plans, headcount plans, and questions about when to open requisitions or how many people to hire as volume grows, shrinks or changes by season. Plans month by month how many requisitions to open so FTE on hand keeps up with FTE needed. A requisition adds capacity only after time to hire a

tools.name: erlang_staffing
tools.description: For call center, contact center, phone or chat staffing questions with a service level target, such as 80% answered within 20 seconds. Works out agents needed on a live queue to answer a target share of contacts within a target time, using Erlang C. Give contacts per hour for the interval being staf

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "required_fte" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "How many people a steady workload needs. Give weekly volume and minutes per case; shrinkage, target occupancy and hours per week fall back to stated defaults. Returns FTE, people to staff (rounded up), every input marked given or assumed, and the arithmetic with numbers filled in. Use hiring_plan wh" → after: "For questions like "how many people do I need" or "how many FTE does this workload take": cases, tickets, claims, orders or any work measured as volume times handling time. Applies shrinkage and target occupancy together; leaving out occupancy understates the people needed by about 15% at the 85% de"

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
